claim: For every tournament \(T\) with at most seven vertices, the integral homology groups of its out-neighborhood complex \(\overrightarrow{\mathcal N}(T)\) are torsion-free. Consequently, any tournament whose out-neighborhood complex has torsion in integral homology has at least eight vertices.
integrity: All tournament isomorphism classes through order seven are generated recursively, with counts independently matching McKay’s catalogue. Every neighborhood chain complex is reconstructed, its boundary-square relation is checked, exact Smith normal forms compute integral homology, and mod-2 ranks provide an independent cross-check.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is a complete finite cutoff through seven vertices, not a general torsion-freeness theorem. It does not classify full seven-vertex homotopy types. An obscure or unindexed later computation under directed-Hom terminology remains a residual literature risk.
title: No torsion in tournament neighborhood homology through seven vertices
